content: 1. Dosing Adjustments for Renal Impairment: For patients with creatinine clearance (CrCl) between 10-50 mL/min, reduce the dose of Penicillin G aqueous by 25%. For patients with CrCl <10 mL/min, reduce the dose by 50-70%. Hemodialysis removes Penicillin G aqueous; administer the drug after dialysis sessions. 2. Neonatal Dosing: Neonates <7 days old and weighing <2000 g: Administer 100,000 units/kg/day intravenously (IV) divided every 12 hours. Neonates <7 days old and weighing >2000 g: Administer 150,000 units/kg/day IV divided every 8 hours. Neonates >7 days old and weighing <1200 g: Administer 100,000 units/kg/day IV divided every 12 hours. Neonates >7 days old and weighing 1200-2000 g: Administer 150,000 units/kg/day IV divided every 8 hours. Neonates >7 days old and weighing >2000 g: Administer 200,000 units/kg/day IV divided every 6 hours. 3. Infants and Children: For infants and children weighing <45 kg: Administer 250,000-400,000 units/kg/day IV divided every 4 hours, not exceeding 24 million units/day. 4. Infections: Moderate infections: Administer 25,000-50,000 units/kg/day IV or intramuscularly (IM) divided every 6 hours. Severe infections: Administer 250,000-400,000 units/kg/day IV or IM divided every 4-6 hours, not exceeding 24 million units/day. 5. Drug Interactions: Live Vaccines: Penicillin G aqueous reduces the efficacy of live bacterial vaccines (e.g., BCG, cholera, typhoid). Avoid coadministration and wait until antibiotic therapy is complete before administering live vaccines. Tetracyclines: Drugs like doxycycline, minocycline, and tetracycline may antagonize the bactericidal effects of Penicillin G aqueous. Avoid or use alternative drugs. Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: Penicillin G aqueous may interfere with the therapeutic effects of drugs like atezolizumab, avelumab, balstilimab, nivolumab, pembrolizumab, and others. Use caution and monitor closely. Amifampridine: Co-administration may increase the risk of seizures due to a lowered seizure threshold. Monitor closely and modify therapy as needed. Amiloride: Penicillin G aqueous may increase the effects of amiloride, potentially causing hyperkalemia. Use caution and monitor potassium levels. Aspirin and Salicylates: Co-administration may increase the levels of either drug due to competition for plasma protein binding or reduced renal clearance. Monitor closely. Oral Contraceptives: Penicillin G aqueous may reduce the efficacy of oral contraceptives by altering intestinal flora. Use caution and consider additional contraceptive methods. Probenecid: Increases Penicillin G aqueous levels by competing for renal tubular clearance. Use caution and monitor. Diuretics (e.g., hydrochlorothiazide, furosemide): May increase Penicillin G aqueous levels by reducing renal clearance. Monitor closely. Macrolides (e.g., azithromycin, erythromycin): May reduce the efficacy of Penicillin G aqueous through pharmacodynamic antagonism. Monitor closely. Fostemsavir: Inhibits OATP1B1/3 transporters, potentially increasing Penicillin G aqueous levels. Avoid coadministration or adjust dosing. Pretomanid: Inhibits OAT3 transporters, increasing Penicillin G aqueous levels. Monitor for adverse effects and adjust dosing as needed. 6. Special Considerations: Penicillin G aqueous may alter the metabolism of certain drugs (e.g., sodium picosulfate) by affecting colonic bacterial flora, reducing drug efficacy. Monitor and adjust therapy as needed. Co-administration with immune checkpoint inhibitors (e.g., durvalumab, cemiplimab) may reduce their therapeutic effects. Use caution and monitor closely. Penicillin G aqueous may increase the toxicity of certain drugs (e.g., amifampridine) or reduce the efficacy of others (e.g., live vaccines, immune checkpoint inhibitors). Adjust therapy and monitor for adverse effects. This interpretation provides a detailed, professional summary of the dosing regimens, drug interactions, and clinical considerations for Penicillin G aqueous, ensuring clarity and precision for medical professionals.
